description: Energy of one decode step of each architecture's reduced vehicle: logic energy from the activity-annotated sign-off power at the routed parasitics (results/physical_abi3/asap7/signoff/*.json), memory and link energy from the per-byte terms of configs/hardware/technology.json applied to the bytes the RTL campaign's memory ports actually move in that step.  ASAP7 is a predictive 7 nm academic PDK; none of these joules may be scaled to a foundry node (docs/METHODOLOGY.md section 9).

qwen3_8b_rom_reticle.description: Reduced Qwen3 on the hardwired decode core, weights in mask ROM, KV and vector memory in on-die SRAM; one step at position 15 (tools/rtl_hdc_decode_campaign.py single step).

memory.name: weight ROM
memory.basis: one 64-lane BF16 word (128 B) per wrom_re cycle

memory.name: program and constant ROM
memory.basis: 1,024-bit instruction per prog_re, 64-bit constant pair per crom_re

memory.name: KV SRAM
memory.basis: kv_re reads one 16-lane FP32 word per lane group (4 x 64 B); kv_we writes one FP32 element; writes charged at the read energy

memory.name: vector memory SRAM
memory.basis: one FP32 element per read-port enable bit; a matrix-engine write is one 16-element line per group (upper bound: the mask can be partial)

mac.basis: results/rtl/hdc_decode_campaign.json weight_macs_per_token (BF16 x BF16 products into FP32 accumulators)

hbm_comparator.description: The same core and step with weights and KV streamed from HBM: the KV streamer (ot_hdc_kv_stream, 4 pseudo-channels = 1/8 of an HBM3E stack) is signed off; the HBM path (device, PHY, controller) is charged the analytical model's measured per-byte energy on the weight and KV bytes the core consumes, plus the stack's idle interface power pro rata.

memory.name: weights from HBM
memory.basis: the core's weight-word reads, each streamed from HBM

memory.name: KV from HBM
memory.basis: the KV bytes the core consumes (the streamer fetches each once into its window; the tail SRAM holds the open tile)

static.name: HBM interface idle
static.basis: 4 of an HBM3E stack's 32 pseudo-channels (tools/rtl_hdc_kv_stream_campaign.py NPC)

deepseek_v41_rom_array_die.description: Reduced DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one die of the ROM array (ot_hdc_core_v41), one step at position 7.  Logic: the routed matrix engine and V4.1 units, activity from the campaign's RTL register activity mapped onto their flops; the sequencer, stream unit, hc projection and Sinkhorn unit have no retained route and are listed as missing.

logic.name: block-dot lanes (16)
logic.note: lane 0's activity for all 16 lanes (lane 15 is analysed to bound the spread)

missing: sequencer, V4.1 stream unit (ot_hdc_v41_stream), hc projection (ot_hdc_v41_hcproj) and Sinkhorn unit: no retained route (being routed by the full-chip workstream); their energy is not in the logic total

memory.name: ROM (weights, expert weights, hc, block-quantised, Engram, constants)
memory.basis: port widths of ot_hdc_core_v41 (HNL=3 hc lanes x 32 bit, BL=16 x QLB=272 bit, 264-bit Engram row, 1,536-bit instruction)

memory.name: KV and vector memory SRAM
memory.basis: one FP32 element per element-port enable bit, 32 elements (128 B) per wide-port enable, one 16-element line per matrix-engine group write (masks ignored: an upper bound)

mac.basis: 64 BF16 weights per matrix-engine ROM word, each one MAC (enable-high cycles of wrom_re and ewrom_re)

deepseek_v41_rom_array_package.description: One package of the DeepSeek-V4.1 ROM array: four dies as one tensor group on UCIe, plus the package's fabric logic.  Die energy is one die-step (four dies each do a quarter of the matrix work in about a quarter of the time; the replicated vector work is not counted); fabric logic is vectorless (default 0.1 input activity, propagated), which overstates idle fabric; the UCIe bytes follow the Qwen package campaign's tensor-split rule (two all-reduces of the hc x dim FP32 residual per layer, each die sending its partial to the three others), derived, not simulated for V4.1.

logic.name: four-die tensor group (one die-step equivalent)
logic.note: four dies each doing a quarter of every matrix for about a quarter of the step spend about one die-step of energy; the replicated vector work (norms, residuals, RoPE) on the other three dies is not counted, so this is a lower bound on the dies

memory.name: UCIe die-to-die all-reduce
memory.basis: 4 dies x 3 peers x 2 all-reduces per layer x 40 layers x (4 hc x 160 x 4 B) = 2,457,600 B per package per token
